headline: Approved $200,000 soil cleanup at 448 High Street, and asked for a draft ban on black plastic takeout containers.
summary: The meeting honored the Congregational Church of West Medford Sanctuary United Church of Christ, which closed after 154 years. Members approved a Comcast conduit at 75 Riverside Avenue, funding for turnout gear and soil cleanup, and a draft ban on black plastic takeout containers. The McCormick Avenue land sale went to committee, and the Law Department funding request was cut.
decisions: Approved resolution honoring the Congregational Church of West Medford Sanctuary United Church of Christ, 7-0.
Approved request for a cost analysis of longer vacation time for city employees, and referred it to the Administration and Finance Committee, 7-0.
Approved resolution supporting Tufts resident assistants in their contract negotiations, 7-0.
Approved request for a draft ordinance on black plastic takeout containers from the Energy and Environment Committee, and referred the item to the Public Health and Community Safety Committee.
Approved a grant of location for Comcast to install underground conduit at 75 Riverside Avenue, with the engineering division's conditions, 7-0.
Approved common victualler license for Pavement Coffeehouse at 177 College Avenue, 7-0.
Referred to the administration a request for an update on the Veterans Department vacancy, 7-0.
Referred the linkage fee updates to the Community Development Board, 7-0.
Approved legal settlements of $5,000 each with Frank Pavaleo and Vivian Wright.
Approved $45,470 for firefighter turnout gear and $200,000 for soil cleanup and reporting at 448 High Street, 7-0.
Approved moving $57,870 in school repair funds to the Brooks and Missitug elementary school repair projects, 7-0.
Referred the city charter update request to the Department of Elections and to the mayor, 7-0.
Referred the order to sell two McCormick Avenue parcels to the Committee of the Whole, with amendments, 7-0.
Approved sending a comment letter to the MWRA Cambridge and Somerville sewer overflow project team, 6-1.
Tabled the request for capital and stabilization funds for the police chief search.
Approved cutting the Law Department's supplemental appropriation request and asking the mayor for an outside review engagement letter and timeline, 7-0.
Approved board and commission appointments dated September 15th 2026.
discussion: Tufts resident assistant contract: Members supported the RAs' bargaining, which the union said involves proposed cuts to housing, meal swipes, and stipends. The union reported a tentative agreement on the first year and said the university wants a mediator for the rest.

Law Department funding: Members argued over whether to keep paying the department's requested funds, and some wanted to keep only staff salaries until an outside review was done. The mayor's offer of an outside review was discussed, with no administration representative present.

McCormick Avenue parcels: Members discussed selling two city lots for affordable housing, and a neighbor said residents had not been told. Members sent the item to a committee that would invite the assessor and housing staff.

Black plastic takeout containers: Members supported a draft ordinance after the Energy and Environment Committee urged restaurants to switch to clear plastic. A resident asked the city to also address other plastics, and members noted an existing styrofoam ban.

Mystic River sewer overflow letter: A commission member said the proposed plan is progress and urged a focus on overall water quality. Members debated whether to ask for a stronger plan, and the letter was approved 6-1.
